title: What do we measure for a regular hexagon?
description: To find the area of a regular hexagon, the video joins the centre to all six corners and gets six identical triangles. Each triangle needs a side and the distance from the centre to that side, so those are the two measurements to take.
teaching_notes: One idea: split a regular polygon into identical triangles from its centre, so the area needs only the side and the distance from the centre to a side. Watch for students who say the distance to a corner is the height.

source: Figure it Out (area of any polygon, question 3)

maths_rules: joining the centre of a regular hexagon to its six corners gives six identical triangles
each triangle has a side of the hexagon as its base
the height of each triangle is the perpendicular distance from the centre to that side
area of the hexagon = 6 × 1/2 × side × distance from the centre to a side
so the side length and the perpendicular distance from the centre to a side are enough
video_script.design: One regular hexagon all video. The centre is joined to the corners, one triangle is read for its base and height, and the six are added. No numbers are given, so the answer is the list of measurements.
